To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
enhancers can be linked to target genes using a number of approaches.
enhancers can regulate gene expression at a distance by interacting with the promoter of their target gene, but the precise mechanisms of enhancer function remain unclear.

we can use epigenomic data to predict the function of distal regulatory sequences, we can use chromatin conformation capture to directly map interactions between enhancers located at long distances from their target genes, we can use correlation-based approaches to infer enhancer–promoter interactions from epigenomic data, and we can use reporter assays and genome engineering to experimentally test the function of enhancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of enhancer–promoter interactions in gene expression regulation and disease.
understanding enhancer function in the context of development and disease, and we hope that this review will provide useful guidance for researchers interested in this area.
understanding the role that distal regulatory elements play in the regulation of gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
enhancers are a major component of gene regulation and that the field of enhancer biology is still in its infancy.
the field is in a state of flux.
we have a long way to go before we fully understand how enhancers regulate gene expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
enhancers are not only important for understanding the regulation of gene expression but also for understanding the mechanisms of disease.
enhancers can regulate gene expression by interacting with promoters and/or by influencing the activity of promoters and/or gene transcription.
enhancers are not mysterious entities but can be identified genomewide and can be functionally linked to target genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
enhancers are complex and that it is essential to understand how enhancers function at the molecular level if we are to fully understand their roles in development and disease.
enhancer function can now be studied systematically and that this knowledge is essential for understanding the role of enhancer dysregulation in disease and for developing new therapeutic approaches.
the function of individual regulatory elements can be determined by combining epigenomic and transcriptomic methods, followed by experimental perturbation of enhancer–target gene interactions.
